claims.text: The baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy undergoes multiple primary non-eutectic crystallization events.
The baseline alloy exhibits a multistep crystallization sequence under rapid and slow cooling procedures.
Extensive primary phase formation occurs in the baseline alloy even under rapid cooling.
Adding approximately 1–3 at.% boron will increase amorphous retention in the alloy.
Adding approximately 1–3 at.% boron will increase the alloy's thermal stability.
Boron will disrupt the nucleation of primary crystalline phases during solidification.
Boron will inhibit primary crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Boron is expected to segregate to incipient crystal nuclei or interfacial boundaries.
Boron segregation will reduce local atomic mobility.
Reduced local atomic mobility will impede formation of critical nuclei for primary crystallization.
Boron will disturb the alloy's local chemical and topological order.
Disturbance of local chemical and topological order will lower the driving force for crystalline-phase nucleation.
Delayed nucleation will widen the supercooled liquid region.
Delayed nucleation will elevate the thermal stability of the retained amorphous phase.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit a wider supercooled liquid region in DSC scans than the unmodified alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will show suppression or delay of multiple primary crystallization peaks relative to the unmodified alloy.
The anticipated effect is limited to the upper end of the studied cooling-rate regime, where some amorphous material is normally retained.
The anticipated effect applies during reheating through the temperature range that triggers primary crystallization in the unmodified alloy.
